fields.v: Liu, T., Dai, D., Du, Y., Yang, Z. (2026). From Dead Code and Static Requirements to Working Engines: Software Revival with Coding Agents. arXiv:2609.36161v1 [cs.SE], 28 Sep 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2609.36161v1 [cs.SE], marked 'Preprint.'; no published venue stated (LLM-use statement refers to ICLR's policy, but no acceptance is stated)
Tsinghua University; UCLA (academic)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — ReviveBench benchmark with two task families (10 software-revival tasks with contamination controls, 13 clean-room engine-reconstruction tasks) graded by hidden verifiers; 8 models from 3 vendors compared under the Claude Code harness; audit of 28 verifier defects and three proposed verifier-validation checks

No SDD approach evaluated. Harness: Claude Code run headlessly (version not stated), with a local protocol adapter for non-Anthropic models. Models: Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5 (Anthropic endpoint or Amazon Bedrock); GPT-5.6 sol, luna, terra; GLM-5.3 flash. Baseline: no-agent run per task. Ablation: Opus 5 reasoning-effort levels (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Additional demonstrations with Fable 5.1: plcforge multi-module toolchain built in three phases, and reconstructed engines used as tools

Reconstruction input: a specification (public standards plus task-specific requirements) and three worked examples; existing implementations forbidden. Revival input: the broken repository (for deleted-module tasks also the paper, README and remaining code). plcforge demonstration: architecture with machine-checkable interface contracts. Output: working code in the agent's workspace

Agent run: headless agent in an isolated sandbox with its own virtual environment, fixed turn budget per task and wall-clock limit; hidden verifier scores the result (anti-cheat checks on forbidden packages, downgraded dependencies, modified tests). plcforge: (1) architecture with interface contracts (12 turns, $6.02), (2) implementation (81 turns, $20.56), (3) repair from CI-style symptoms only (80 turns, $12.50). Verifier audit loop: defect detected, fixed, re-score or re-run
None during agent runs (headless). Humans (authors) audit the verifiers after runs: achievability probe, candidate consensus, recomputation of self-reported diagnostics

23 tasks: 10 revival (e.g. PyMOL 2.3 C++ build, QuPath 0.2.3 Java platform, Caduceus GPU model; 3 post-cutoff repositories) and 13 reconstruction engines with 4 to 43 verifier checks each. plcforge: six modules, 7,520 lines of Python. Reconstruction solver sizes 134 to 1,560 lines (CFD task). 215 runs (excluding GLM-5.3 flash), 155 valid; GLM adds 33 runs, 13 reported

Tasks: 10 revival and 13 reconstruction tasks. Configurations: Claude Code harness with 3 models (revival) or 8 models from 3 vendors (reconstruction); non-Anthropic models through a local protocol adapter. Baseline: no-agent run per task. Held constant: harness, fixed turn budget per task identical across models, hidden verifiers, isolated environments; wall-clock limits not uniform across batch scripts; adapter strips a protocol flag for GPT-5.6 (changes tool set). Acceptance tests: hidden verifiers with task-level pass thresholds. Repetitions: most cells one or two seeds, best eligible run reported; unequal numbers of attempts. Human intervention: none during runs

Revival: Fable 5.1 restores 10/10, Sonnet 5 8/10, Haiku 4.5 4/10; obfuscation lowers similarity without lowering any model's pass rate; post-cutoff Fable 5.1 8/9 runs. Reconstruction: Fable 5.1 and Opus 5 13/13, Sonnet 5 10/13, GPT-5.6 sol 9, GLM-5.3 flash 7, luna 6, terra 5, Haiku 4.5 2. Fable 5.1 averages 20.8 turns per engine vs 74.1 for Opus 5; cost does not track capability (Sonnet 5 $35 for 10 engines vs Opus 5 $76 for 13). MES and PLM passed by all models (non-discriminating); CFD task does not establish solver capability. No significance tests

Partly: it separated models on most engines, but two tasks (MES, PLM) do not discriminate and the CFD verifier awarded full marks to a 134-line program with no numerics (false positive). Repeatability not established: authors state results do not establish stable model rankings, pass probabilities or robustness to thresholds. Limitations stated: 28 verifier defects (24 false negatives, 2 false positives), one or two seeds per cell with best-run selection, author-chosen thresholds, cost not comparable across vendors, harness corrections for GLM-5.3 flash, turn budgets can decide outcomes

Limitations: small samples and best-run selection; thresholds chosen by the authors; cost not comparable across vendors (adapter pricing artifact); GLM harness corrections and missing output cap in early runs; non-uniform wall-clock limits; unreliable turn counts for failed runs; non-discriminating tasks; CFD verifier graded a self-reported quantity. Gaps: executable verification itself introduces substantial measurement error; reliable evaluation needs validation of grading logic and execution conditions (achievability probes, independent self-tests, recomputed diagnostics, confirmation that settings are enforced); new revival benchmarks should use post-cutoff repositories and obfuscated controls

Inconsistencies: run counts do not add up (215 runs = 155 valid + 37 gateway/quota errors leaves 23 unexplained; the 6 budget-exhausted runs are not placed). Table 3 gives Opus 5 9 valid runs while it passes 13 engines, each needing at least one valid run. Revival claim 'our conclusion provides meaningful suggestions for software design' is not supported by the results. Harness version and turn budget values (other than 120 turns for Sonnet 5 on revival) not stated. Values from Table 1 (revival), Tables 2-3 (reconstruction, rebuilt from jumbled extraction and cross-checked with Figure 2a and Section 6 text) and Table 4 (ablation). Data: reproducibility statement says task definitions, verifiers, trajectories and scripts are archived and released with the benchmark, and 'Codes can be found in this repo', but no link is given. No pre-registration. Programming languages: Python (most tasks, plcforge), C++ (PyMOL), Java (QuPath)
